notice: RN bank batch 144: Pediatric case studies: infant dehydration, nephrotic syndrome, glomerulonephritis and Wilms tumor. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings of significant dehydration.

rationale.correct: A 9% weight loss with tachycardia, sunken fontanel and poor output is moderate to severe dehydration.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Using the Holliday-Segar method (100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg), what is this infant's daily maintenance fluid requirement based on the usual weight of 9 kg? Record your answer in mL/day.

rationale.correct: 100 mL x 9 kg = 900 mL/day, about 38 mL/hr, before replacing the deficit.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Because the infant is becoming sleepy with slow capillary refill, the priority is {{b1}}, and the best fluid is {{b2}}.

options.text: a 20 mL/kg bolus of 0.9% sodium chloride

rationale.correct: IV isotonic bolus for severe signs.

perOption.b1:c: Too much sugar, too little sodium.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: After the bolus, the infant is more alert. Which parts of the plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give clear apple juice and flat soda to settle the stomach
Give loperamide to slow down and stop the diarrhea

rationale.correct: ORS in small amounts, diaper weights, early feeding and potassium after voiding.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: 1 hour
exhibits.body: Heart rate 140/min. Refill 2 seconds. Voided once.

questions.stem: Which infection control actions should the nurse take for rotavirus? Select all that apply.

options.text: Contact precautions with gown and gloves
Hand washing with soap and water
Dedicated equipment such as a stethoscope
Teach that rotavirus vaccine prevents severe disease in siblings
Share toys with other children in the playroom

rationale.correct: Contact precautions, soap and water, dedicated equipment and vaccination.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action for rotavirus infection control.

exhibits.title: Day 1
exhibits.body: Stool test: rotavirus positive. Infant missed the rotavirus vaccine.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement by the parent, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll give ORS after each loose stool."
"I'll come back if there are fewer than 4 wet diapers a day."
"I'll keep feeding the usual formula."
"I'll dilute the formula with extra water to be gentle."
"I'll give homemade salt water if we run out of ORS."

rationale.correct: ORS replacement and warning signs; never dilute formula.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings of nephrotic syndrome.

rationale.correct: Massive proteinuria, low albumin, high lipids and edema.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it fits nephrotic syndrome or acute glomerulonephritis.

rows.text: Heavy protein, no blood in urine
Cola-colored urine with red cells
Hypertension
Very low albumin and high cholesterol
Recent strep throat

rationale.correct: Protein and edema versus blood and hypertension.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The main treatment is {{b1}}, and the child is at risk for {{b2}}.

rationale.correct: Prednisone; watch for infection and clots.

perOption.b2:a: Loss of antibodies and anticoagulant proteins.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Urine dipstick for protein each morning
Skin care and turning, supporting the scrotum
Room with a child who has chickenpox

rationale.correct: Weights, dipsticks, skin care and salt limits.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Prednisone 2 mg/kg/day. No-added-salt diet. Daily weight.

questions.stem: On day 5, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Prepare for cultures and IV antibiotics
Check vital signs and perfusion often
Increase the prednisone dose without an order

rationale.correct: Fever with abdominal pain in nephrotic syndrome suggests spontaneous peritonitis.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.educationalObjective: Take action on infection in nephrotic syndrome.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement by the parent, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll test the urine each morning and call if it shows protein for 3 days."
"I'll give prednisone in the morning with food."
"We'll avoid live vaccines while on high-dose prednisone."
"I'll stop the prednisone when the swelling goes."
"Increased appetite and a round face are side effects of the medicine."

rationale.correct: Home testing, correct steroid use and no live vaccines.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate its cause in APSGN.

rows.text: Red cells and casts in the urine
High blood pressure
Periorbital edema
Low complement
Headache

rationale.correct: Immune injury reduces filtration and causes fluid retention.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Admit. Fluid restriction to insensible losses plus output. Furosemide.

questions.stem: On day 2, the child says the light hurts the eyes and vomits. Review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the room quiet and dim
Give an IV antihypertensive as prescribed
Encourage the child to drink to replace the vomit
Let the child play in the playroom

rationale.correct: Headache, photophobia and vomiting with high BP suggest encephalopathy.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: At 2 weeks, for each finding or statement, indicate whether it shows recovery or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Blood pressure 104/66 mm Hg
Urine output normal
Microscopic blood in the urine
"Next time, we'll have sore throats tested and finish antibiotics."
Rising creatinine

rationale.correct: Most children recover fully; rising creatinine needs evaluation.

perOption.r5:c1: Not expected; may not be APSGN.
perOption.r5:c2: Not expected; may not be APSGN.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that support Wilms tumor.

rationale.correct: A firm flank mass in a well-appearing preschooler suggests Wilms tumor.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it fits Wilms tumor or neuroblastoma.

rows.text: Smooth flank mass that does not cross the midline
Irregular mass that crosses the midline
Raised urine catecholamines
Associated with aniridia
Bruising around the eyes from orbital spread

rationale.correct: Features help separate the two common abdominal tumors.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The most important nursing rule before surgery is {{b1}}, because {{b2}}.

options.text: do not palpate the abdomen; post a sign at the bed
palpate the mass each shift to measure it
bathe the child with vigorous scrubbing
rupture of the capsule can spread tumor cells

rationale.correct: No palpation; handle gently.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Which parts of the preoperative plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Age-appropriate preparation with dolls or pictures
Abdominal palpation teaching for the parents
Delay surgery until after a month of play therapy

rationale.correct: BP, gentle handling, preparation and kidney tests.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The parent cries and says, "I should have noticed it sooner." Which responses are therapeutic? Select all that apply.

options.text: "These tumors are often silent; you found it."
"Would you like our family support team?"
"Yes, a careful parent would have seen it earlier at bath time."
"Don't cry in here; your child will see you upset and get scared."

rationale.correct: Reduce guilt, reflect and offer support.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: After nephrectomy, for each finding, indicate whether it is expected or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Urine output 1.5 mL/kg/hr
Bowel sounds absent with a distended, tender abdomen on day 3
Pain controlled with scheduled medicines
Blood pressure back to normal
Temperature 38.9 C during neutropenia from chemotherapy

rationale.correct: Recovery; bowel obstruction and fever with neutropenia need action.

exhibits.body: Stage II Wilms tumor; favorable histology.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 9-month-old infant (usual weight 9 kg) has had vomiting and watery diarrhea for 2 days. Rotavirus is spreading at the infant's daycare. The infant has had one wet diaper in 12 hours.

exhibits.title: Admission
exhibits.body: A 4-year-old child has had puffy eyes in the morning for a week and now has swelling of the legs and scrotum. The child is tired and has a poor appetite.

exhibits.title: Pediatric clinic
exhibits.body: A 7-year-old child had a sore throat 2 weeks ago that was not tested. Today the child has puffy eyes, a headache and dark urine.

rows.label: Urine
cells: Cola-colored, red cells and red cell casts

exhibits.title: Clinic
exhibits.body: A parent noticed a firm swelling on one side of a 3-year-old child's abdomen while bathing the child. The child is otherwise playful.

rows.label: Abdomen
cells: Firm, smooth mass on the right flank; does not cross the midline

rows.label: Eyes
cells: No iris present (aniridia) in the right eye

rows.label: CT
cells: Right kidney mass, suspected Wilms tumor

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
